newsitem.title: INDIA: India shares drift lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: India shares drift lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: Indian shares drifted lower on Monday with participants unwilling to make fresh commitments after a big fall on Wall Street, traders said.
"Very lacklustre," said one dealer at a big institutional brokerage house. "I can't see anyone building positions. People are concerned. They will stay on the sidelines."
A holiday at the Bombay and Delhi bourses also contributed to the sluggish activity, he said.
Asian Paints bucked the trend after Britain's Imperial Chemicals Industries Plc (ICI) said it has bought a 9.1 percent stake.
The share rose 24.30 rupees, or 7.4 percent, to 353.80.
A Bombay-based finance firm Kotak Mahindra Capital Company said it had purchased the shares from the Choksey family, one of four original promoters of Asian Paints.
"Thereafter, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company has agreed to sell these shares to ICI Plc at 351 rupees per share subject to approvals," it said in a statement.
Asian Paints is ICI's main competitor in India.
Three other promoters have about 40 percent of Asian Paints equity with Indian financial institutions and domestic investors holding the balance, analysts said.
The Madras index eased 40.81 points, or 0.91 percent, to 4,421.13 and the Calcutta index 1.51, or 1.25 percent, to 119.36.
Analysts expect the market to open subdued on Tuesday.
"The Dow Jones tumble has affected the mood," said S.N. Satish, a fund manager at Lloyds Finance. "Fund managers are going to put fresh purchases on hold."
The market was unlikely to see a sell-off though, he said.
On Friday, the Dow Jones had slumped 247.37 points, or 3.1 percent, to 7,694.66 on a weakening dollar and worries of corporate earnings.
